It must be uploaded to the learning portal by 4 pm on 5 December. Paper copies are not accepted. The portal sends you a receipt by email when your upload is complete, and you should keep this as proof of submission. We strongly recommend uploading a day early, as the portal can be slow in the final hour before a deadline. Work handed in late will lose 5 marks for each day it is late, for up to three days. After that it will receive a mark of zero. If something outside your control, such as illness or a family emergency, stops you from meeting the deadline, you can request an extension using the extension form on the portal. Requests must be made at least 48 hours before the deadline, except in a genuine emergency, and must be approved by your personal tutor. Anyone who has not booked by then will be given a slot automatically, which may not be at a convenient time. You may bring printed boards or present from a laptop, but the room projector must be tested with a technician on the Friday before. 4.4 How your grade is worked out Your final grade is made up of two parts: the portfolio counts for 60% and the presentation for 40%. The pass mark for the course is 50. If you do not pass, you may resubmit your portfolio once, in March, but the mark for a resubmitted portfolio will be capped at 50. Grades are released on the portal about four weeks after the presentations, and every student receives written feedback from both panel members. 4.5 Peer feedback sessions Throughout the term there are four peer feedback sessions, in which small groups share work in progress and comment on each other's ideas. These sessions are compulsory and count towards your attendance. Past students have told us that these sessions were among the most useful parts of the course, and many have kept in touch with their groups long after finishing. A final word on wellbeing: the end of term can be a busy time, and it is easy to leave everything until the last week. Tutors are always happy to look at drafts during tutorials, and the college library runs quiet study evenings on Wednesdays. Over the last eighteen months many of you took part in our hybrid working pilot, filled in surveys and joined the focus groups run by the People Team. Thank you. We had more than 300 responses, and they have shaped the policy below. Our leadership group signed it off last week, and it will apply to all staff from 6 January. A full copy is on the intranet; this message covers the main points. Before we get into the details, a little background. The pilot showed that most of you value the flexibility of working from home for focused work, but that teams missed the chance to meet in person, and new starters in particular found it harder to learn from colleagues. The policy tries to keep the best of both. It has been discussed with the staff forum and with each department head, and we have made several changes in response to their comments, including the extra support for home equipment described below. Time in the office Everyone is expected to work from the office at least two days a week. One of those days must be your team's anchor day, when the whole team is in together. For most teams this will be Tuesday, but some teams, such as Finance and Customer Support, will choose a different day because of their workload. Your line manager will confirm your team's anchor day by the end of this month. The second office day is up to you, as long as you agree it with your manager. If you would like to work a different pattern, for example three days in the office or a compressed week, please fill in the flexible working form on the intranet and send it to your line manager by 13 December. Requests to work fully remotely will still be considered, but these need to be approved by the People Team as well as your manager, and will usually only be agreed for specific roles or personal circumstances. Desks and booking We are moving to shared desks on both floors. From 6 January, there will be no fixed desks, and you will need to book a desk through the desk booking system at least 24 hours in advance. Lockers will be available for personal items and can be requested from reception. Please clear your current desk of all personal belongings by 20 December, when the cleaning team will start preparing the floors. Anything left after that date will be boxed up and taken to the post room. Core hours To make sure people can reach each other, everyone should be available between 10 am and 3 pm on working days, wherever they are working from. Outside these hours, you can arrange your day as suits you and your team. Please keep your calendar up to date so colleagues can see when you are in the office and when you are at home. Home working support Every member of staff working at least one day a week from home will receive a home working allowance of £25 a month, paid with your salary, to help with the cost of internet and heating. It will be paid automatically from the January payroll, so you do not need to apply. In addition, you can request one monitor, a keyboard and an office chair for use at home by completing the equipment request form. These remain company property and must be returned if you leave. Working from other locations Working from somewhere other than your home or the office, such as a holiday home or a family member's house, is fine for short periods. However, working from another country for more than 10 working days in a year needs approval from both your manager and the People Team, because of tax and insurance rules. Please ask well in advance. Reviewing the policy We know this is a big change, and we do not expect to get everything right straight away. We will run a short survey in June and review the policy after six months. Your feedback during the pilot was invaluable, and we want to keep hearing from you. Our director, Mohammed Aziz, will host an open question session on 10 December at 2 pm in the main meeting room and online, and all staff are welcome. If you have any questions in the meantime, please speak to your manager or email the People Team. We would much rather hear your concerns now than after the policy has started. Best wishes,
Ingrid Solberg
Head of People

Keep the dishwasher clean and follow the instructions in the manual to look after it properly.

7.1 Cleaning the filter The filter at the bottom of the tub catches food particles so that they are not sprayed back onto your dishes. It should be cleaned once a week, or more often if you do not rinse plates before loading them. Turn the cylindrical filter anticlockwise and lift it out, then remove the flat mesh plate underneath. Rinse both under warm running water, using a soft brush to remove any grease. Never use a metal scourer or wire brush, as this can damage the mesh. Refit the mesh plate and lock the filter by turning it clockwise until you hear a click. The dishwasher must never be used without the filter in place. 7.2 Rinse aid and salt The rinse aid indicator on the control panel will light up when the rinse aid needs refilling, usually about once a month. Open the dispenser cap next to the detergent compartment and fill it to the MAX line, then wipe away any spills, as these can cause excess foam. If your water is hard, you will also need to add dishwasher salt to the container at the bottom of the tub when the salt indicator comes on. Use only salt made for dishwashers; table salt contains additives that may damage the water softener. When filling the salt container for the first time, add one litre of water before adding the salt. 7.3 Spray arms Once a month, check that the holes in the upper and lower spray arms are not blocked. The lower arm can be pulled straight up; the upper arm is released by unscrewing the nut in the middle. Clear any blocked holes with a cocktail stick and rinse the arms under the tap before refitting them. Make sure both arms turn freely by hand afterwards. 7.4 Maintenance wash To remove grease and limescale from inside the machine, run an empty maintenance wash on the 70°C programme once a month, with a dishwasher cleaner or a cup of white vinegar placed upright on the top rack. Doing this regularly also helps prevent unpleasant smells. 7.5 Outside and door seal Wipe the door seal and the edges of the door with a damp cloth every week to remove food residue. Clean the control panel and outside of the appliance with a soft, damp cloth only; do not use sprays, bleach or abrasive cleaners, as these can mark the finish. After each cycle, leave the door slightly open for a short while to let moisture escape. If your dishwasher is not going to be used for several weeks, for example while you are away on holiday, clean the filter, run a maintenance wash and leave the door slightly open. If you notice a fault that is not solved by the steps above, please see Section 8, Troubleshooting, before contacting the service centre.
